learningObjectives: Learning objective: describe translations, rotations and reflections accurately, distinguish their effects on orientation and use clockwise and counterclockwise correctly.
Translation: A shift sending all points through the same displacement.
Rotation: A turn of a specified angle about a chosen center.

activityMap.correct: About 120° counterclockwise about fixed vertex O; all corresponding distances preserved
activityMap.equivalent: 2π/3 radians counterclockwise or a reasoned estimate near 120° before precise measure
activityMap.malformed: Missing angle, center or justification without diagram

activityMap.correct: Moves in order: translate (+2,0), rotate 90° clockwise about P, reflect across horizontal line y=0 through P, translate (0,+2), rotate 90° counterclockwise about P; vertex ordering flips ONLY at the reflection
activityMap.equivalent: Clear written/oral exact inverse-compatible descriptions and congruent labelled diagrams
activityMap.wrong: Calling frame 3→4 a translation/rotation or claiming unchanged handedness
activityMap.malformed: Missing a frame, ordered vertex label, mirror line or partner evidence

activityMap.correct: Cards 1/4 translations, 2/6 rotations, 3/5 reflections; name vectors/centers/lines and justify orientation change
activityMap.equivalent: An oral grouping with valid geometric justification is as acceptable as written explanations
activityMap.wrong: Classifying a reflection as rotation just because tip unchanged
activityMap.malformed: Only category names without grouping and reason

activityMap.correct: P'(-1,1), Q'(-3,1), R'(-2,3) is the x=0 reflection; P''(-1,1), Q''(-3,1), R''(2,3) is NOT that reflection
activityMap.equivalent: Perpendicular bisector of corresponding pairs is x=0, equal distances and unchanged y, explanation by coordinates or geometric constructions
activityMap.wrong: Saying second triple is reflection across x=0 or omitting R correspondence

privateTeacherRubric.Scoring: Each R1–R4 scores 0 absent/incorrect; 1 partly correct with incomplete justification; 2 fully correct and evidenced. Teacher records criterion-by-criterion notes offline.

Criteria.Skill: 2.1 accurate source-relevant counterclockwise 120° rotation estimate, fixed center O, mathematical reasoning
2.2 five precise transitions in six frames with chirality reversed on only frame 3→4, documented partner reconstruction
2.3 six-card correct grouping with translation vector, rotation center/angle or reflection line justification
First-party Cool-down reflection x=0 with point pairs/equal distances and valid negative counterexample

teacherKey.rotation: 120° CCW about O (angle estimate within reasonable drawing/measurement error accepted when justified), all four distances preserve; not a 90° turn
frames: 3→4 reflect about y=0, P and tip R remain fixed, Q crosses line (positive chirality to negative)
teacherKey.cooldown: Yes first image across x=0; no second image, because R″=(2,3) is on wrong side and wrong mirror distance.

correct: Activity 2.1 120° CCW about O with justification

equivalent: Activity 2.1 two-thirds π radians CCW with fixed O

boundary: Angle is estimated: a mathematically justified approximate reading near 120° need not be exactly 120.00°
Correct physical half-turn and -180°/180° equivalence for Card 6 should not be rejected
Tip direction alone cannot decide reflection; compare non-collinear ordered vertices
Handedness preserved under rotations/translations and reversed only under reflection
Different oral vs written wordings are equivalent when fully geometrically reproducible
